analysis.title: Earnings Tracker Week 3: Plenty of beats, Big Tech takes the heat
key_insights: With 301 S&P 500 companies reported (2/3 of index earnings), 75% beat on EPS, 70% on sales and 58% on both. That compares with 77%/72%/61% at this point last quarter and historical post-Week 3 averages of 66%/60%/47%.

3Q S&P 500 EPS growth is tracking +28% YoY but has been revised up by only 1% since October 1. Excluding one-time charges at Meta (litigation) and Alphabet (SpaceX revaluation), the revision would be +3%, below the +4% at this point last quarter.

Hyperscalers showed no sign of cutting capex. Meta, Alphabet and Amazon signaled significant growth in 2027, and Microsoft signaled acceleration in the first half of CY2027 as delayed third-party capacity arrives. All but Microsoft generate negative FCF, and investors punished softness: Alphabet fell more than 12% after missing on Search.
Hyperscalers and Semis together lost more than $800bn in market cap last week, roughly the value of the smallest 67 S&P 500 companies combined.
Breadth is healthy. Median EPS growth is tracking +12% YoY (2Q: 14%), and 79% of stocks are on track to grow EPS YoY (2Q: 81%), still above the 90th percentile historically.
Upward revisions to 4Q and 2027 S&P 500 EPS (+1-2% in October) came entirely from Tech and Energy. Excluding them, 4Q EPS was cut 1% and 2027 was roughly flat.

Guidance is stronger than usual: 2.3x as many above- as below-consensus EPS guides in October versus an October average of 1.0x. Excluding Tech the ratio is 1.8x. Consumer sectors and Utilities show the weakest guidance trends.
Week 3 reactions were larger, with five TMT stocks moving +/-20% or more. The beat/miss spread stayed the lowest since 2001: beats outperformed by 0.4ppt the next day and misses by +0.1ppt.
Reddit and Intel beat 3Q EPS but fell nearly 30% on weak guidance. AI disruption weighed on Reddit and higher memory prices hurt Intel's PC business.
October dispersion was driven by rotation out of Momentum and Growth into Value and Cash Deployment. FCF/EV was the top factor at +11%, 99th percentile versus the equal-weighted S&P 500 since 1986.

S&P 500 capex grew 37% YoY in 2Q26, the strongest pace in the data history. Consensus implies about +50% in 3Q, and +10% excluding Tech and the Mag 7. Hyperscaler capex is expected to grow more than 90% in 2026 and about 50% in 2027, and to exceed operating cash flow until the back half of 2028.

Earnings quality is weaker. NTM FCF relative to net income is below normal because of hyperscaler capex. Investment revaluations at Amazon and Alphabet added about $150bn to 2026 net income, and contributed nearly 20ppt to 2Q S&P 500 EPS growth (+50%, or +32% ex-gains).

BofA card data show spending per household up 6% YoY in the week ending Oct 24 (+5% ex gas). Lower-income spending growth has outpaced higher-income growth for several weeks. Gas spending is up about 25% YoY.

The effective tariff rate has settled near 7% after the repeal of IEEPA tariffs. About $150bn of an estimated $165bn eligible refunds has been paid, a 0-5% boost to 2026 GAAP S&P 500 EPS. Economists see risk of re-escalation if the midterms produce gridlock.
FX turned from a tailwind to a headwind in 3Q, cutting sales growth by about 0.2ppt (DXY +2% YoY).
BofA expects 2027 EPS of $410 (+12%) versus bottom-up consensus of $424 (+16%), and sees 2027 risks skewed to the downside. Its 3Q26 estimate is $93.50 (+32%) versus consensus $91.03 (+28%).
Small caps: 58% beat on EPS, 46% on sales and 34% on both, weaker than last quarter. Mid caps: 62%/56%/40%. Small-cap 3Q EPS is tracking 2% below the start of October and mid-cap 4% above.
Week 4 is the last big reporting week, with about 140 companies including Apple and Palantir (11/2), AMD (11/3), and McDonald's, Qualcomm and Uber (11/4).

market_movers.rationale: Alphabet fell more than 12% after missing on Search. A SpaceX revaluation reduced 3Q EPS by about 20%. Full-year 2026 capex guidance of $195-205bn is unchanged, with a significant increase expected in 2027.
Reddit beat 3Q EPS but fell nearly 30% on weak 4Q guidance, with AI disruption weighing.
Intel beat 3Q EPS but fell nearly 30% on weak guidance. Higher memory prices pressure its PC business, and it expects 2026 PC unit TAM down about 12%.
A one-time litigation charge weighed on 3Q EPS revisions. Management expects to keep investing aggressively beyond 2026.
Calendar-2026 capex is now about $170bn versus $175bn prior on third-party capacity delays. Spending is expected to accelerate in the second half of the fiscal year.
Management expects 2026 cash capex of about $220bn and meaningfully more in 2027.

sector_views.rationale: Guidance is strongest in Info Tech, and the sector accounts for 79.5% of 2027 consensus S&P 500 EPS growth. Semis drive 61.9%.
Energy has driven upward estimate revisions, with 3Q consensus EPS growth of +145.6% YoY.
Weak guidance and revision trends. Only 62% beat on EPS, the lowest of the large sectors.
Worst 2027 EPS revisions in October, and guidance trends are among the weakest.
Weakest guidance trends alongside consumer sectors. Only 50% beat on sales.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 3Q26 EPS growth is tracking +28% YoY on bottom-up consensus ($91.03), and consensus net income growth is 31% on current constituents. BofA's own 3Q26 estimate is $93.50 (+32%), as of 10/30/2026.
301 of 500 S&P 500 companies have reported: 75% beat EPS, 70% beat sales, 58% beat both (reported results).

Tech has the best beat rates at 94% on EPS and 91% on sales. Semis and Tech Hardware beat EPS 100%. Consumer Discretionary is weakest at 62% on EPS and 52% on sales, and Materials lowest at 59% on EPS.
Consensus 2027E S&P 500 EPS is $424 (+16%) versus 2026E $364 (+33%). BofA forecasts $410 (+12%) for 2027 and $365 for 2026.

Alphabet's full-year 2026 capex guidance of $195-205bn is unchanged. Microsoft expects Q2 capex above $50bn and about $170bn for calendar 2026 versus $175bn prior. Amazon expects about $220bn of 2026 cash capex.
Intel guided to a 2026 PC unit TAM decline of about 12% (second-half units down more than 20%) and 2027 TAM down 10% on a unit basis because of memory.
Meta's 3Q EPS was hit by a one-time litigation charge. Alphabet's was hit by a SpaceX revaluation that detracted about 20% from its EPS.
Week 4 reporters include AAPL, PLTR, VRTX and MAR (11/2), AMD, AMGN, ANET and PFE (11/3), MCD, QCOM, UBER, CVS and APP (11/4), and COP, ABNB and MNST (11/5).

A 0-5% boost to 2026 GAAP S&P 500 EPS if fully recognized.
Consensus tracking, revised up just 1% since October 1.
BofA sees downside risk to consensus.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A stronger dollar (DXY +2% YoY) turned FX into a headwind.

risk_factors: Hyperscaler cash burn: all but Microsoft have negative FCF, and capex is expected to exceed operating cash flow until the back half of 2028.
Earnings quality: one-time investment revaluation gains at Amazon and Alphabet boosted EPS and could reverse.
Upward revisions are concentrated in Tech and Energy, and ex-those sectors 4Q EPS was cut 1%.
Memory prices are pressuring PC demand, per Intel.
Consumer weakness in furniture and department stores, and downside risk from geopolitical conflict.
Higher cost of capital and rate pressure on 2027 earnings.
Tariff re-escalation if the midterms produce gridlock.

geopolitical: Unresolved geopolitical conflict poses downside risk to 4Q and 2027 consumer sectors.
Heightened geopolitical uncertainty has persisted and is driving energy prices higher (Mastercard comment).
Midterm gridlock in Washington could lead the administration to re-escalate trade tensions.
Geopolitical bottlenecks and a higher cost of capital could disrupt the AI-driven earnings story.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers signal no tempering of capex, with 2027 spending set to grow significantly. Consensus expects AI-exposed revenue growth to close the gap with capex growth.
tension_points.bear_case: All but Microsoft generate negative FCF, capex is expected to exceed operating cash flow until the back half of 2028, and investors punished any softness (Alphabet down more than 12%).
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further upward capex revisions without matching AI revenue growth, or softness in cloud and search results.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus has 2027E EPS at $424 (+16%), with 2027 EPS revisions positive in October and guidance strong (2.3x).
tension_points.bear_case: BofA forecasts +12% ($410), with risks skewed to the downside from rates, commodity pressure and geopolitics. Ex-Tech and Energy, 2027 estimates are flat.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A higher cost of capital and geopolitical bottlenecks hitting Tech would undermine the bull case.
